title: DiffAdapt: Difficulty-Adaptive Reasoning for Token-Efficient LLM Inference
why: Closest prior work: trains an MLP probe on frozen-backbone post-prefill hidden states to select an Easy/Normal/Hard reasoning configuration -- the same frozen-probe-for-allocation mechanism this paper's M2 uses -- but never benchmarks the probe against large-model self-report and never reports a matched-dollar-budget accuracy-per-dollar frame (its currency is token savings at preserved accuracy); grounding is digest.md N3 item 1 / N4 item 1, not a separately cached PDF. [Phase-A-followup 2026-07-04: real arXiv mirror found (2510.19669, ICLR 2026) and full N0-N12 digest built from the actual PDF, replacing the corpus-motivation-only stub.]

title: Adaptive Thinking: Large Language Models Know When to Think in Latent Space
why: Closest prior work alongside DiffAdapt: trains a 2-layer MLP on the prefill final-token hidden state to predict a self-consistency score and gate extended chain-of-thought -- directly anticipates this paper's M2 (probe) and M1b (self-consistency) signals -- but treats self-consistency as the supervision target rather than as a competing controller, and never compares against self-report or a matched-dollar budget; grounding is digest.md N3 item 2 / N4 item 1, no separately cached PDF. title: CaTS: Calibrated Test-Time Scaling for Efficient LLM Reasoning
why: Rival design point on the same problem: obtains one-pass calibrated confidence by fine-tuning the base model itself (confidence distillation), which this paper's frozen-backbone premise explicitly rejects -- unavailable for API models/shared serving stacks and charges training cost to every new backbone (digest.md N4 item 2); no PDF cached locally for this OpenReview-only submission; a stub digest (motivation+method verbatim from openview_corpus/ideas.jsonl) was built for this reference-cache upgrade, corroborating digest.md N3 item 3.

title: DiSRouter: Distributed Self-Routing for LLM Selections
why: Rival operationalization of self-report: trains every model in a cascade with SFT+RL to answer-or-forward, conceding in its own motivation that 'intrinsic self-awareness is... not sufficiently calibrated... for routing-quality decisions' -- the per-model training investment this paper's frozen-probe premise is designed to avoid entirely (digest.md N4 item 3); cross-model cascade routing, not within-model tier choice; no PDF cached locally for this OpenReview-only submission; a stub digest (motivation+method verbatim from openview_corpus/ideas.jsonl) was built for this reference-cache upgrade, corroborating digest.md N3 item 4.

title: TRIM: Hybrid Inference via Targeted Stepwise Routing in Multi-Step Reasoning Tasks
why: Routes at reasoning-step granularity using a separately trained process-reward model to decide per-step regeneration -- a compute-allocation controller, but scoped to decomposable multi-step math traces rather than generic per-query allocation, and its own controller carries nontrivial per-step inference cost unlike this paper's near-zero-cost probe (digest.md N4 item 4); no PDF cached locally for this OpenReview-only submission; a stub digest (motivation+method verbatim from openview_corpus/ideas.jsonl) was built for this reference-cache upgrade, corroborating digest.md N3 item 5.

title: Evidence for Limited Metacognition in LLMs
why: Behavioral evidence that models' delegate-game choices poorly exploit their own internal confidence ('self-reports may be largely imitative rather than evidential') -- the direct evidentiary basis for this paper's skepticism toward self-report as a reliable, decision-quality controller (digest.md N4 item 5, N2 motivation) -- but it neither prices the elicitation call nor compares self-report against internal-state probes as budget-constrained controllers; no PDF cached locally for this OpenReview-only submission; a stub digest (motivation+method verbatim from openview_corpus/ideas.jsonl) was built for this reference-cache upgrade, corroborating digest.md N3 item 6.

title: Beyond Speedup - Utilizing KV Cache for Sampling and Reasoning
why: An alternative frozen-feature design (pooled KV-cache tensors instead of hidden states) for the same difficulty-estimation task, motivated by hidden-state probing's memory/deployment cost -- adjacent evidence that frozen internal signals other than raw hidden states also carry routing-relevant information -- but its comparison set is other hidden-state/trajectory-search methods, not self-report or training-free signals under one matched budget (digest.md N4 item 6); no PDF cached locally for this OpenReview-only submission; a stub digest (motivation+method verbatim from openview_corpus/ideas.jsonl) was built for this reference-cache upgrade, corroborating digest.md N3 item 7.

title: Beyond Linear Probes: Dynamic Safety Monitoring for Language Models
why: Extends linear activation-space probes to incrementally-evaluable Truncated Polynomial Classifiers for safety monitoring, motivated by the overhead of LLM-based monitors -- adjacent evidence that probe compute can itself be made to scale dynamically -- but it classifies harmfulness, not expected correctness/difficulty, so it is not a compute-allocation controller (digest.md N4 item 7); no PDF cached locally for this OpenReview-only submission; a stub digest (motivation+method verbatim from openview_corpus/ideas.jsonl) was built for this reference-cache upgrade, corroborating digest.md N3 item 8.

title: RouterArena: An Open Platform for Comprehensive Comparison of LLM Routers
why: An open evaluation platform for routers that choose between models (not within-model compute tiers), with metrics for cost/optimality/latency at that granularity -- the model-choice counterpart this paper's within-model tier-choice comparison is explicitly scoped against (digest.md N4 item 8, paper.md 'out of scope'); no PDF cached locally for this OpenReview-only submission; a stub digest (motivation+method verbatim from openview_corpus/ideas.jsonl) was built for this reference-cache upgrade, corroborating digest.md N3 item 9.
